title: Gochujang-Glazed Fried Chicken Sandwich with Kimchi Slaw
summary: Buttermilk-marinated, double-fried boneless skin-on chicken thighs tossed in a sticky gochujang glaze, stacked in a toasted milk bun with garlic Kewpie mayo, kimchi slaw and quick-pickled jalapeños.
notes: Video: 'The Perfect Fried Chicken Sandwich' on the Joshua Weissman Recipes channel (UCUAg71CJEvFdOnujmep1Svw). Written recipe: https://www.joshuaweissman.com/recipes/perfect-fried-chicken-sandwich-recipe (serves 8, prep 30 min, cook 1 hour). Marinating (at least 1 hour, ideally overnight) and cooling the pickles are not in prep_minutes (house rule 13). The video states nearly every amount; the written recipe supplies the chicken (2 lb bone-in thighs, about 6-8), the slaw's 2 green onions, the onion powder (captions garbled), the bun count (6-8; 8 used to match 8 servings) and gram weights for flour, starch, gochujang and MSG. He does not bake buns in this video. The pickled jalapeños, chicken sauce, garlic mayo and slaw are kept as groups in this recipe. The chicken is entered as bought, bone-in (2 lb chicken-thigh-bone-in, house rule 12); he debones it, and the lead converts to edible weight. Our estimates: 65 g per bun, 1/8 tsp salt for 'a tiny pinch' in the mayo, 2 1/2 cloves for '2-3 cloves', and 1.25 g/ml for sweet soy sauce. Coatings: the buttermilk marinade is not poured off; after the chicken comes out, 1/2 cup of dredge and the baking soda are whisked into it and it becomes the wet dip, so the whole marinade counts at 50% as a wet batter, and the dredge counts at 29.7% because 1/2 cup of it goes into the dip (house rule 3; arithmetic in each line). This is a large share for a buttermilk dip (much of it is left in the bowl; he says it covers up to eight pieces and could be reused), so the coating may be overstated. Frying oil: 3-3 1/2 quarts (vegetable, canola or avocado; canola-oil stands in for 'vegetable oil'); the pot is excluded and 107 g absorbed oil is counted at 10% of the raw coated weight, using the as-bought chicken weight (125 g). Pickle brine (water, vinegar, salt, sugar), the jar's garlic and dill are not counted; all 5 jalapeños are counted (USDA's 14 g pepper understates his very large ones). House rule 10: the chicken sauce (about 1 cup) is a tossed glaze and nothing says it is all used, so 50% is counted. The garlic mayo (1 cup, about 2 Tbsp per sandwich, spread on both buns) and the slaw (sized for the sandwiches: 'you only need about two cups', mixed just before assembly) are made for these 8 sandwiches and treated as used up, so they count in full; if leftovers are expected, 50% would apply. Dark soy sauce uses regular soy sauce; Kewpie uses regular mayonnaise; milk/brioche buns use a plain hamburger-roll proxy (fat understated). The written recipe marks the kimchi optional; the video uses it, so it is counted. The written recipe's first fry is at 300°F; the video says 325°F (the video wins). Pepper in the mayo and salt in the slaw are to taste and not counted.

steps.text: Debone the thighs, keeping the skin: follow the fat line on the underside with your knife to expose the bone, scrape along it with the back or tip of the blade, then cut it free at both ends. Check for leftover cartilage.

Marinade: whisk the buttermilk, hot sauce, white pepper, gochujang, MSG, kosher salt, sugar and garlic powder until the gochujang dissolves. Add the chicken, massage it in, cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.

Pickled jalapeños: bring the water, vinegar, salt and sugar to a boil until dissolved. Pack the sliced jalapeños into a pint jar, pour the hot brine over to cover, and press a piece of plastic wrap or paper towel on top to keep them submerged. Cool to room temperature, add the crushed garlic and dill, close and refrigerate.

Chicken sauce: whisk the gochujang, ketchup, dark soy, sweet soy, honey and vinegar, boil in a small pot over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, then take it off the heat. Once the bubbling stops, stir in the minced garlic so it stays mostly raw.
Garlic mayo: whisk the Kewpie mayonnaise with the MSG, grated garlic, a tiny pinch of salt and black pepper.
Core the cabbage and slice it paper-thin on a mandoline; you need about 2 cups. Refrigerate it unmixed until assembly so the slaw does not go watery.
Dredge: whisk the flour, potato starch, kosher salt, MSG, cayenne, garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper.

Lift the chicken out of the marinade and let the excess drain. Whisk about 1/2 cup of the dredge and the baking soda into the leftover marinade to make a dip, then flick a few spoonfuls of the dip into the dredge and stir to form small crunchy clumps.
With one wet and one dry hand, coat each thigh in the dip, then press it firmly into the dredge, including under the skin, until there are no bare spots.

Heat 3-3 1/2 quarts of high-heat oil to 325°F in a 7-quart pot and fry 1-2 pieces at a time until cooked through. Then raise the oil to about 350°F and fry each piece again until crisp and golden. Drain.
Slaw: squeeze the kimchi hard to remove its liquid and chop it roughly. Toss with the cabbage, sliced green onion, grated garlic and Kewpie mayo, gently, by hand.
Toss the fried chicken in the gochujang sauce until coated. Toast the buns cut side down in butter in a nonstick pan over medium heat until golden.
Build each sandwich: bottom bun, garlic mayo, slaw, glazed chicken, pickled jalapeños, more mayo and the top bun.
